$comment: Single source of truth for every agent in this harness. setup-harness-loop.mjs generates ALL THREE runtimes from it: .kiro/agents/*.json (kiro-cli), .claude/agents/*.md (Claude Code) and .codex/agents/*.toml (Codex CLI). Edit this file, then re-run setup with --force, or `node harness/tools/gen-agents.mjs --target .`. Never hand-edit the generated agent files — verify-harness reports agent-generated-stale. Field mapping: prompt -> kiro `prompt` file:// URI / Claude system-prompt body (inlined at generation); resources -> kiro `resources` / Claude SubagentStart hook injecting them as additionalContext (computed at spawn, so never stale); writes -> kiro toolsSettings.write.allowedPaths / Claude PreToolUse hook denying edits outside the list / Codex project-level PreToolUse hook in .codex/hooks.json, which learns the role from the HARNESS_AGENT env var because Codex agent TOML has no per-agent hooks field (Claude has no per-agent path permission field, and an Edit(...) rule in settings.json is session-wide, so the hook is the only per-agent enforcement); trace -> lifecycle hooks; model -> per-runtime model, null meaning "the runtime default". Evaluator roles (checker, design-facilitator) get the strongest model available because their whole job is to catch what a cheaper model produced — design-facilitator only gets one deep pass now instead of a cheap generator plus a reviewer loop, so it runs on the strongest model rather than the executor tier `designer` used to; executors run cheap. kiro offers no Opus on this account (kiro-cli chat --list-models), so its evaluators use claude-sonnet-4.5, the strongest it has. Executors are PINNED to claude-sonnet-4 rather than left on kiro's `auto`: on 2026-08-12 `auto` returned "temporarily unavailable" mid-run and killed a maker part-way through a fix. `auto` is a router, not a model, and it can route to nothing. Codex models: evaluators get gpt-5.6-terra with high reasoning effort (OpenAI's own reviewer example); executors get gpt-5.6-sol, the documented default. `codex debug models` lists sol/terra/luna with no cost or capability ordering, so no cheaper tier is guessed for executors — a wrong guess there downgrades the role whose job is catching what a cheaper model got wrong. `subagentAllExceptSelf: true` (kiro only, verified against kiro.dev's subagents docs 2026-08-18) generates `toolsSettings.subagent.availableAgents` as every other agent name — it mechanically backs prompts/orchestrator.md's 'never spawn the orchestrator itself' MUST NOT instead of leaving it prompt-only, on the one runtime that has a native in-session subagent tool to gate.

agents.name: orchestrator
agents.description: The human-facing front door: reports loop state, natively spawns the node harness/loop/route.mjs names, and escalates decisions. Uses scripts only as a fallback; does not choose nodes or write product files.
agents.welcomeMessage: Reports where the loop is, spawns the next sub-agent the router names, and brings decisions to you. It never picks the node itself.

agents.name: checker
agents.description: Checker in the maker-checker loop: re-runs evidence, tries to falsify, and is the only agent allowed to set status=done. Write-restricted to state files.

agents.name: design-facilitator
agents.description: Turns a requirement into a design by sharpening a human's thinking, not by deciding for them: named components and boundaries, a claims table where every fact is cited or spiked, a registry of load-bearing assumptions, at least two real options with an argument map each, and a structured self-applied critique (Key Assumptions Check, premortem, Devil's Advocacy, steelman gate). Never sets status=approved — that is the human's alone, recorded in loop/design-approval.json.
agents.welcomeMessage: Design facilitator: point me at the requirement. I generate at least two real options — each with an argument map, not just a support chain — before I ever ask which you're leaning toward, so I don't anchor on your first instinct. I build the claims table, the assumption registry, and the seams/invariants, then run a structured critique on the option you lean toward: Key Assumptions Check, premortem, Devil's Advocacy for the option you're NOT leaning toward, and a steelman gate before any objection of mine appears. I never write status: approved — only you do, in loop/design-approval.json, and if you override a concern of mine I record it as an accepted risk rather than dropping it.

agents.name: feature-planner
agents.description: Turns a raw requirement into a right-sized, dependency-ordered feature_list.json. Runs once at setup (and again only when scope changes enough to need re-planning) — not a per-iteration loop role like maker/checker.
agents.welcomeMessage: Feature planner: point me at the requirement (a file, or describe it) and I'll decompose it into a right-sized feature_list.json — build features for named components, prove features mapped to acceptance scenarios, sized so one maker iteration can finish each. I don't implement anything.

agents.name: harness-setup
agents.description: Set up and validate the harness against the real environment: toolchain, MCP connectivity, real verification commands, and a green ./harness/init.sh baseline. Setup only — no feature work.
agents.welcomeMessage: Harness setup: I will verify the toolchain, confirm MCP connectivity, fill in the real verification commands, and get ./harness/init.sh green. Setup only — no feature work.

agents.name: maker
agents.description: Maker in the maker-checker loop: advances exactly one feature by one step per iteration with honest evidence. Cannot set status=done.

agents.name: test-designer
agents.description: Turns the spec into test conditions WITHOUT reading the implementation. The independent oracle: designs what must be true, so the test cannot become a transcript of the code it judges.

agents.name: test-implementer
agents.description: Turns validated test conditions into running test code, red first. Writes tests only — never the implementation they judge.

agents.name: k8s-integration-tester
agents.description: Stands up the project's Helm chart in an isolated namespace, writes and runs real Level-3 (microservice integration/contract) tests against it, and diagnoses failures via read-only cluster access. Never runs helm/kubectl directly itself — tools/k8s-test-env.sh is the only thing that deploys or tears down. A specialized maker: cannot set status=done.
agents.welcomeMessage: K8s integration tester — here's what I do, in order: (0) check the cluster is reachable and start it myself if it's a local minikube/kind that's down (never touch a shared cluster's lifecycle); (1) read/write docs/testing-standards.md's Level 3 definition; (2) point tools/k8s-test-env.sh at the real Helm chart; (3) write a real test that exercises the deployed service over the network, not a mock; (4) run it through the script — I never run helm/kubectl myself, only read-only diagnosis; (5) on failure, read dumped diagnostics + the read-only k8s-readonly MCP server, fix, retry; (6) wire the confirmed command into docs/testing-standards.md; (7) stop a local cluster again when k8s work is done, so it doesn't starve your other test suites. I record evidence like a maker — I cannot set status=done myself, the checker does. Tell me the chart path (or the requirement, if there's no chart yet) to start.
